summary: Jörg Plassen specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He has served as a professor at Geumgang University and was attested as a professor at Ruhr University Bochum in 2013.

Jörundur Garðar Hilmarsson was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Oslo, the Sorbonne, and Leiden (PhD 1986), under Werner Winter, and taught at the University of Iceland from circa 1986 to 1992.

Jørn Borup worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Aarhus University in 2002 under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, later serving there as associate professor from circa 2008 to 2023.

Júlia Szivák works in Indology and linguistics. Educated at Corvinus University, Eötvös Loránd University, Central European University, and Birmingham City University (PhD 2021), she held posts at Eötvös Loránd University and as a Leverhulme Early Career Research Fellow at Nottingham.

Jürgen Hanneder is an Indologist who studied at Munich, Bonn, and Marburg (PhD circa 1996) under Alexis Sanderson and Michael Hahn. He worked at Halle-Wittenberg before becoming a professor at the University of Marburg in 2007.
Jürgen Neuß specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Harry Falk and completed his doctorate at the Free University of Berlin in 2007.

Jürgen Renn works in history, archaeology, and philosophy, earning his PhD from TU Berlin in 1987. He directed the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (1994) and became director at the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology in 2022.

K. A. Nilakanta Sastri was a historian and Indologist who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He held posts at Annamalai University, the University of Madras (Professor, circa 1929–1946), and the University of Mysore.

K. A. Subramania Iyer studied Indology, linguistics, and philosophy at London and Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Lionel David Barnett. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Lucknow University (1921–1960) and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1960–1962).
K. Ammini Amma is an Indology scholar who conducted research at the University of Madras, where she is attested as a research student in 1940 and 1971.
K. Balasubramania Iyer was an Indologist who served as managing editor of the Journal of Oriental Research and was attested as secretary of the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute in 1945.
K. Jayakumar is an Indologist and linguist educated at St. Joseph's Higher Secondary School, Thiruvananthapuram. He served in the Indian Administrative Service from circa 1978 to 2012.
K. Kanapathypillai was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Hartley College and the University of London from circa 1933 to 1936, and taught Alvappillai Veluppillai.

K. Kunjunni Raja was an Indologist and linguist who earned doctorates at Madras and London under C. Kunhan Raja, Thomas Burrow, and John Brough. In 1951, he became Professor and Head of Sanskrit at the University of Madras.

K. L. Dhammajoti is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kelaniya under Yinshun and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa. He taught at Kelaniya and held leadership posts at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Hong Kong.

K. Madhava Krishna Sarma was an Indologist who studied under C. Kunhan Raja. He was affiliated with the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1940, 1971) and served as curator of the Anup Sanskrit Library (attested 1946).
K. Meenakshi is an Indologist and linguist who completed a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under M. A. Mehendale. She was attested at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 1983.

K. Munirathnam is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under N. S. Ramachandra Murthy. He served as Director (Epigraphy) I/c at the Archaeological Survey of India, attested from 2013 to 2018.

K. N. Jayatilleke was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under O. H. de A. Wijesekera and Ludwig Wittgenstein at Cambridge. He served as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon from circa 1953 to 1963.

K. N. Neelakantan Elayath worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as assistant professor at Government Arts College (1967–1969) and Sree Krishna College (1972–1984), and as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calicut (1990–2003).
